results.policy_response: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC, part of GCHQ) issued a formal statement on 4 August 2026 — the day AISI disclosed the incident, and one week after AISI notified the NCSC and the Government Cyber Co-ordination Centre — from its Chief Technology Officer Ollie Whitehouse, responding to 'recent incidents resulting from frontier AI evaluations' and calling for strong safeguards, real-time oversight and pre-planned incident response rather than reliance on after-the-fact detection. NCSC followed it on 20 August 2026 with interim guidance, 'Managing the cyber risk of agentic AI', which opens by citing the recent incidents of AI models and agentic systems 'carrying out unsanctioned or unintended activity' and sets out network-isolation, compute-isolation, credential-scoping, observability and emergency-shutdown maturity models pending formal guidance that will supersede it. Both are advisory regulator publications, not binding instruments.
